A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MFSWB research, with v2 adding 'Towards' to the title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian simulations, ShapeNet point-cloud averaging, color harmonization, and MNIST autoencoder experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Gaussian learning-rate experiments and CIFAR10/STL10 autoencoder results, including appendix Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The constrained MFSWB formulation, three surrogate objectives, slicing distribution, gradient estimators, and Algorithms 1–4 are retained. The latent-distribution formula is corrected to match the already-described encoder regularization; the MNIST architecture is reformatted rather than replaced.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates autoencoders only on MNIST; v2 adds CIFAR10 and STL10 in Tables 5–6, extending evaluation from handwritten digits to RGB natural images. Gaussian, ShapeNet, color-harmonization, and MNIST coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain USWB, formal MFSWB with lambda 0.1, 1, and 10, and the three surrogates; autoencoder comparisons also retain conventional SWAE. New benchmark tables reuse this set. Their 'UBSW' and 'MFBSW' spellings are label transpositions, not additional methods.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the original MNIST reporting with per-metric best results from a learning-rate search and adds image-space fairness evaluation. CIFAR10/STL10 introduce 500-epoch protocols, latent dimensions 48/128, and FID-based image metrics. Gaussian experiments add learning-rate settings. The exact MNIST grid is inconsistent: Section 4.4 includes 0.0008, Table 2 omits it, and Appendix D retains the earlier 0.01 setting.

E4.justification: New Figure 5 tests Gaussian-barycenter sensitivity to learning rates 0.001, 0.005, and 0.05, supplementing the original 0.01 experiment. Existing lambda sensitivity studies, convergence comparisons, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: The three-independent-run statement in Section 4.2 and the uncertainty entries in Tables 1 and 3 are unchanged. Revised and added autoencoder tables report point values without a new seed count, uncertainty estimate, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces MNIST values under the new search protocol; for example, es-MFSWB's reported latent fairness value, scaled by 100, changes from 0.98 to 1.760. These are not same-setting performance comparisons. v2 also adds image-fairness scores, CIFAR10/STL10 results, and Gaussian learning-rate outcomes. Point-cloud Tables 1 and 3 remain numerically identical.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 corrects the class empirical measure from atoms at raw samples Xki to atoms at encoded samples f_phi(Xki), fixing its latent-space support. Appendix Equations 17–19 additionally define FID-based evaluation quantities. Propositions 1–6 and the existing proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: constrained marginal fairness, three tractable surrogates, their theoretical relationships, and empirical benefits. Added benchmarks support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies v1's blanket preference for es-MFSWB by distinguishing its latent-space fairness from us-MFSWB's image-space fairness and discussing variability in latent Wasserstein rankings. The natural-image discussion extends the existing fairness-versus-reconstruction tradeoff to the added datasets.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link on the first page and documents training settings for CIFAR10/STL10, including learning rate, epochs, regularization weights, and latent dimensions. The existing MNIST architecture and hardware disclosures are retained, with the architecture consolidated into Table 4.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting CIFAR10, STL10, FID, and proposed future extensions using generalized and augmented sliced Wasserstein distances. Appendix C retains the same substantive distinction between marginal fairness and prior demographic-parity work.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and author information, copyedits several passages, expands explanations of pushforwards and sorting permutations, and moves references before the appendices. The main section sequence and argumentative structure remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially resizes and regroups retained displays. It extends Table 2, converts the architecture listing into Table 4, and adds Figure 5 and Tables 5–6. Existing qualitative results are retained despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the empirical argument by testing natural-image autoencoders beyond MNIST, measuring image-space fairness, and examining learning-rate sensitivity. Its interpretation also distinguishes the surrogates' strengths more carefully. These are useful gains, but conflicting MNIST learning-rate descriptions and per-metric selection complicate interpretation of the revised Table 2, limiting the overall improvement.
